definitions.explanation: Two or more people having or wearing the same design of item, deliberately matched. Most often used of clothes or accessories.

examples.japanese: {姉妹|しまい}でお{揃|そろ}いの{服|ふく}を{着|き}る。
このカップは{夫婦|ふうふ}でお{揃|そろ}いだ。
examples.english: These cups are a matching pair for the couple.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{旅行|りょこう}の{記念|きねん}にお{揃|そろ}いのキーホルダーを{買|か}った。
examples.english: My friend and I bought matching keychains as a souvenir of the trip.

notes:
From {揃|そろ}う (to match, to be complete) with the polite prefix お〜. Refers to people deliberately having the same item, usually with a friendly or affectionate nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{揃|そろ}いの{服|ふく}: matching outfits
- お{揃|そろ}いにする: to make (items) matching
- ペアでお{揃|そろ}い: a matching pair

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ペアルック: matching couple's outfits — loanword, specifically for couples dressing alike
- {同|おな}じ: the same — plain factual sameness, without the coordinated, intentional nuance

cross_references.label: to be complete, to be uniform
